problems.description: New test file is named test_notification_server.py while the code under test is app.py (a Flask auth API). The module-under-test naming convention is broken, so future sessions/maintenance will not be able to map the test suite to the app it exercises.
test_notification_server.py declares classes that are not PascalCase (per static analysis), violating the repo's Python naming convention.
test_notification_server.py declares module-level constants that are not UPPER_CASE (per static analysis).

Session 1 rewrote the tier-2 seed baseline outright (-247/+213 lines), consolidating the app into a leaner single app.py rather than building incrementally; cognitive complexity rose +1 even as smells fell, so the rewrite is not strictly additive.

strengths: Zero new bugs and zero duplication introduced (bugs +0, duplications +0.0%)
Net reduction of 3 code smells (smells -3), improving overall code health
Expanded the codebase with 3 new files and +19 functions, adding tests alongside the app
Net -34 lines while adding functionality — a lean consolidation
commit_reviews.summary: Session 1 greenfield rewrite trims the auth seed to a leaner app and adds test coverage with zero new bugs and fewer smells, but the test file's mismatched name (test_notification_server.py vs. app.py) and class/constant casing leave convention debt for later sessions.

problems.description: broadcast()/system() semantics are silently overloaded: if the payload contains a 'channel' key they send to only that channel's subscribers, otherwise to all connections. This changes the meaning of the existing broadcast/system protocol for callers who include a 'channel' field, coupling routing decision to payload contents rather than an explicit message type.

Cognitive complexity jumped +26 (SonarQube), concentrated in _handle_message and _handle_http, which are now heavily branched (subscribe/unsubscribe/broadcast/direct/system + three HTTP path shapes with nested parsing). The new feature accounts for nearly all of the added complexity.

Cleanup logic in _handle_client's finally block (discard client + delete empty channel) duplicates _unsubscribe's behavior inline instead of reusing it, so channel-eviction bookkeeping lives in two places.

The /channels/<name>/subscribers endpoint exposes subscriber client IDs over an unauthenticated HTTP route; low severity since IDs are UUIDs but it widens the server's information surface beyond the health count.

Convention score 0.83 per measurement; the two flagged violations (PascalCase class, UPPER_CASE module constant) are in test_notification_server.py and appear pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff's added snake_case functions.

strengths: Feature is architecturally coherent: it slots into the existing message-type dispatch chain, reuses _send_to_connections, and guards all _channels mutation under the existing _clients_lock, matching the module's concurrency pattern.
Channel validation (_message_channel) is defensive — rejects non-string/empty channels and conflicting top-level-vs-payload channel values via the existing ValueError error path.
The /health and new /channels endpoints follow the same response/header construction style, and the new HTTP behavior is covered by tests via a raw-socket helper.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated channel subscribe/unsubscribe feature that follows the server's existing dispatch and locking patterns but introduces technical debt by overloading broadcast/system semantics and adding substantial branching complexity (+26 cognitive complexity).

problems.description: InMemoryBroker and RedisBroker expose an identical async method surface (start/stop/publish/add_client/remove_client/has_client/subscribe/unsubscribe/channel_members/channel_summary) but no Protocol/ABC enforces it; NotificationServer.__init__ takes the union type directly, so a third backend could drift silently.
RedisBroker.remove_client scans every registered channel (smembers over notifications:channels) and issues an srem per channel on every disconnect, making teardown O(channels).

A synchronous sqlite3.Connection is opened in the async server lifecycle without check_same_thread handling; if touched from async handlers it blocks the event loop and may conflict with the monitoring thread the removed RLock comment referenced (usage only partially visible in the truncated diff).
Measured violations in test_notification_server.py: a class not using PascalCase and module-level constants not UPPER_CASE — the two items behind the 0.83 convention score.
Measured cognitive complexity +38; the broker listener and delivery paths could be decomposed into smaller helpers.

strengths: Clean broker strategy with backward-compatible constructor defaults, falling back to InMemoryBroker when Redis is unconfigured.
Correct async lifecycle handling: start/stop symmetry and explicit cancellation of the pub/sub listener task with CancelledError handling.
Modern, well-typed surface: PEP 604 unions and a typed MessageHandler Callable alias on public signatures.
Static analysis reports zero new bugs and 0.0% duplication while preserving the existing NotificationServer surface and server lifecycle.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid integration session that delivers Redis distribution and SQLite history behind a clean broker seam (architectural fit 0.72, convention 0.83, agreeing with the mechanical scores), though the implicit broker interface and an unguarded sync SQLite connection introduce moderate maintainability debt.

problems.description: broadcast() gathers sends with return_exceptions=True but silently discards any exception via an early return, hiding per-connection failures with no logging.

WebSocketTransport._handle_http reaches directly into NotificationServer private members (_broker, _messages) and embeds HTTP endpoint routing in the transport layer, so any future transport must reimplement server-level endpoints; HTTP handling arguably belongs on the server, not the transport.

start() detects 'already running' by probing transport.port and catching RuntimeError — exception-based control flow is convoluted and couples the server to the transport's not-running error contract.
assert self._client_handler is not None guards runtime state but is stripped under python -O; a plain runtime check would be safer.

The two measured convention violations (PascalCase classes, UPPER_CASE constants) are in test_notification_server.py, a file NOT touched by this diff — pre-existing, not introduced by this commit, so the 0.83 score does not penalize the change itself.

strengths: Extracting a BaseTransport ABC decouples NotificationServer from websockets, enabling alternate transports and isolated testing.
Lazy imports inside start()/_handle_http keep the websockets dependency deferred, improving import cost and optional-dependency handling.
stop() properly closes and waits for the transport and resets handler state, keeping lifecycle cleanup symmetric with start().
Type hints and docstrings on public signatures follow project conventions (snake_case, PascalCase, ABC/abstractmethod pattern mirroring the existing broker classes).
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, net-positive transport-abstraction refactor that decouples the server from websockets, with minor debt from swallowed exceptions in broadcast(), server-internal access in the transport's HTTP handler, and exception-as-control-flow in start(); the measured convention violations are pre-existing in an untouched test file.

problems.description: The in-memory rate-limit path grows `_local_rate_limits` unboundedly — entries for distinct client_ids are never pruned, a slow memory leak for long-running instances with many short-lived connections.

The daily TTL cleanup issues a full-table `DELETE ... WHERE timestamp < ?`; the new index is on (channel, timestamp) so its leading column doesn't serve the cleanup scan, which will degrade as the table grows.

The /history request branch adds a dense try/except/else parse-and-validate block (parse_qs + 5-field validation in one shot), which is the likely source of the +19 cognitive complexity and +1 smell delta.
Two convention violations in the test file (a class not in PascalCase and a module-level constant not in UPPER_CASE), per the mechanical measurements; the source file itself is clean.
The new test exercises the configured-limit path; the Redis-broker rate-limit branch (incr/expire) does not appear to be covered separately, so the dual-path behavior lacks equal test coverage.

strengths: Closely mirrors existing patterns: the /history route reuses the established request-dispatch and error-shape style, and the Redis-vs-local rate-limit dual path mirrors the existing broker abstraction.
Parameterized SQL throughout — no injection surface introduced.
The cleanup background task has a clean lifecycle: created in start(), cancelled and awaited in stop().
Adds an index on (channel, timestamp) aligned with the new history query's filter and ordering.
All new behavior ships with tests and configuration via env vars with sensible defaults.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured cross-cutting addition (rate limiting, message TTL, history endpoint) that respects existing dispatch and broker patterns, with only minor maintainability concerns around the unbounded in-memory rate-limit map and the cleanup scan's index fit.

compounding_issues: Binary __pycache__/*.pyc artifacts committed in every session (3 tracked pyc files in the final tree) — diff/repo pollution that grew monotonically and was acknowledged in Session 4 but never cleaned up (no .gitignore, pycache tracked from Session 1 onward)
Single-file monolith: Session 4 extracted transports into classes but left everything in app.py (561 lines final), so the codebase never modularized as features, persistence, and brokers accumulated

HTTP endpoints are coupled into WebSocketTransport._handle_http via the websockets process_request hook — a future SSE/polling transport (the stated point of the abstraction) cannot reuse them, so the transport boundary doesn't fully generalize

Rate limiter charges every inbound message (including malformed and control/subscribe traffic) against the per-client budget before protocol validation, so invalid messages consume the 100/min allowance
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the unrelated Flask-auth seed codebase entirely and greenfielded a websockets.asyncio server rather than reusing the seed
Canonical message envelope {type, payload, timestamp} plus system event/ack protocol established in Session 1 and preserved unchanged across all five sessions

Broker abstraction (InMemoryBroker/RedisBroker) in Session 3 — retained zero-config in-process behavior while adding Redis pub/sub fan-out and set-based connection/channel state for multi-instance deployment
SQLite history table introduced in Session 3, then indexed (composite channel/timestamp) and exposed as paginated /messages and /history endpoints with a periodic TTL cleanup task in Session 5
BaseTransport ABC dependency-inversion refactor in Session 4, decoupling the server from websockets while keeping all 7 prior tests passing with zero changes
Dual wire format for channel targeting (top-level 'channel' or nested in payload) supported and normalized into delivered payloads since Session 2
Dual rate-limit implementations — Redis INCR/expiry when Redis is configured, in-memory sliding window otherwise (Session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. The code grew from a 137-line flat handler into a layered 561-line system (protocol → channels → broker abstraction → transport abstraction → rate limiting/history), with integration tests accumulating 3 → 5 → 7 → 7 → 9 — the pure-refactor Session 4 held steady at 7 with no regression, demonstrating a disciplined, behavior-preserving restructuring. Every increment was validated end-to-end against real websocket clients, fakeredis, and on-disk SQLite. The two test failures that occurred (Sessions 3 and 5) were correctly diagnosed as test-setup deadlocks rather than application defects. The only blemishes are accumulating hygiene debt — committed .pyc binaries and a growing single-file monolith — rather than any functional decay, so the arc is a clean, compounding-quality climb with a slight hygiene plateau at the end.
story_review.summary: A high-coherence, steadily improving five-session build that grew a minimal WebSocket notification server into a layered multi-instance platform through disciplined, fully integration-tested increments, capped by a behavior-preserving transport refactor and a cross-cutting rate-limiting/history session, though punctuated by accumulating hygiene debt in committed .pyc artifacts and a single-file monolith.
